basic_identification.name: Creative coding frameworks
basic_identification.originator: Processing (Casey Reas, Ben Fry, 2001). p5.js (Lauren McCarthy, Processing Foundation, 2014). TouchDesigner (Derivative Inc., Greg Hermanovic, 2000s). openFrameworks (Zach Lieberman, Theo Watson, Arturo Castro, 2005). Hydra (Olivia Jack, 2018). Sonic Pi (Sam Aaron, 2012). Also: Max/MSP (Cycling '74), vvvv, Nannou (Rust), Cinder, cables.gl.
basic_identification.geography: Global. Processing Foundation (USA). Derivative/TouchDesigner (Toronto). Strong communities in North America, Europe, Japan, South Korea, Latin America. Academic hubs at ITP/NYU, MIT Media Lab, Goldsmiths, IMAL Brussels, ZKM Karlsruhe.

core_ideas.core_claim: Creative coding frameworks lower the barrier between programming and artistic expression, making computation a medium for art. Processing's founding principle was making coding accessible for artists, designers, and educators. Each framework embodies a different trade-off between accessibility, performance, and expressiveness.
core_ideas.medium_specificity: Entirely digitally native. These tools exist because digital art requires translating artistic intent into executable code. The specificity lies in making computation itself the creative medium rather than using computers to simulate traditional media. Generative art, interactive installations, live coding performance, and algorithmic composition are practices impossible without these frameworks.
core_ideas.relation_to_attention_economy: Largely resistant to attention economy logic. These are creation tools, not distribution platforms. They do not optimize for engagement metrics. However, the outputs created with these tools enter the attention economy when shared on social media or minted as NFTs. TouchDesigner's prominence in large-scale installations (Refik Anadol) creates spectacle that feeds attention circuits. The frameworks themselves remain infrastructure-neutral.
core_ideas.relation_to_intention: Strongly intention-native. These tools serve the declared need of artists to create computationally. They are built by and for creative practitioners rather than for engagement capture. The Processing Foundation's commitment to inclusivity and education exemplifies intention-alignment. No framework monetizes user attention or data.

market_economics.revenue_model: Processing/p5.js: nonprofit, grant-funded via Processing Foundation, donations. TouchDesigner: free for non-commercial use, commercial licenses from $600+/year. openFrameworks: free, open-source, community-maintained. Hydra: free, open-source. Sonic Pi: free, open-source, educational funding. Max/MSP: commercial license ($399 perpetual or $9.99/month). vvvv: free for non-commercial, commercial licenses required.
market_economics.market_position: Tool layer. These are means of production, not markets themselves. They sit upstream of all digital art creation and downstream of general-purpose programming languages.
market_economics.price_range: N/A for frameworks themselves (mostly free). Art created with these tools ranges from student projects to million-dollar installations. Generative art minted via Art Blocks/fxhash (typically coded in p5.js/JavaScript) has sold for up to several hundred ETH.
market_economics.volume_trend_2024_2026: Stable to growing. p5.js continues expanding its user base through education adoption. TouchDesigner is growing in commercial installation and live performance sectors. The generative art NFT market (often p5.js-based) contracted with the broader NFT crash but the tool communities remain healthy. New entrants like Nannou (Rust-based) indicate continued innovation. [uncertain]
market_economics.collector_demographics: N/A for frameworks themselves. Art created with these tools is collected by: generative art collectors (on-chain platforms), museums and institutions (installations), corporate clients (immersive experiences), and individual collectors across the economic spectrum.
market_economics.sustainability: Highly sustainable as open-source infrastructure. p5.js and Processing are maintained by a nonprofit foundation with diversified funding. openFrameworks survives on community contribution. TouchDesigner has a viable commercial model. The key sustainability risk is maintainer burnout in volunteer-driven projects. The tools have persisted through multiple hype cycles because they serve fundamental creative needs.

practice_aesthetics.toolchain: Processing: Java-based, Processing IDE. p5.js: JavaScript, any browser/editor. TouchDesigner: proprietary node-based environment, GPU-dependent. openFrameworks: C++, various IDEs (Xcode, VS Code). Hydra: browser-based live coding, JavaScript. Sonic Pi: Ruby-based, dedicated IDE. Common auxiliary tools: Git, Shader editors (GLSL), Arduino/hardware integration, OSC/MIDI for interactivity.
practice_aesthetics.relation_to_AI: Complex and evolving. AI is being integrated as a tool within these frameworks: RunwayML plugins for TouchDesigner, ml5.js (machine learning for p5.js), TensorFlow.js integrations. Some artists use creative coding frameworks to build custom AI tools or to visualize/critique AI systems. The frameworks are also used to create art that comments on AI. Tension exists between hand-coded generative art (valorized for human authorship) and AI-generated outputs. Creative coding communities generally maintain that code-as-craft has distinct artistic value from prompt-based AI generation.
practice_aesthetics.liveness: Full spectrum. Static generative images (Processing/p5.js plots). Real-time interactive installations (TouchDesigner, openFrameworks). Live coding performance (Hydra, Sonic Pi, TidalCycles). Evolving/generative systems that change over time. Interactive audience-responsive works. The liveness spectrum is a key differentiator within the creative coding field.
practice_aesthetics.aesthetic_vocabulary: Rich and developing. Generative, algorithmic, procedural, parametric, emergent, noise (Perlin, simplex), flow fields, particle systems, recursive, fractal, glitch, databending, live coding, audiovisual, immersive, interactive, responsive, computational, coded. The vocabulary is more developed for visual aesthetics than for conceptual or critical dimensions. Publications like Creative Applications Network, Processing Foundation blog, and academic venues (SIGGRAPH, NIME, ISEA) contribute to vocabulary development.
practice_aesthetics.tendency_axis_position: Strongly open (most frameworks are open-source). Commons-oriented: shared code libraries, community tutorials, open educational resources. Infrastructure over spectacle at the tool level, though outputs can be spectacular. Mixed individual/collective: individual artistic authorship is primary, but collaborative and community practices (live coding ensembles, creative coding meetups) are significant.

infrastructure_governance.openness: Predominantly open-source. Processing (LGPL), p5.js (LGPL), openFrameworks (MIT), Hydra (AGPL), Sonic Pi (MIT). TouchDesigner is proprietary but offers free non-commercial use. Max/MSP is proprietary. The open-source majority makes this one of the most accessible creative tool ecosystems.
infrastructure_governance.governance_model: Processing Foundation: nonprofit with board governance, community contributors, fellowship programs emphasizing diversity. openFrameworks: informal community governance, core team of maintainers. TouchDesigner: corporate (Derivative Inc.) with active user community input. Hydra/Sonic Pi: founder-led with community contribution. Most projects lack formal governance structures beyond core maintainer teams.
infrastructure_governance.data_sovereignty: Strong. Artists fully own their code and outputs. No platform lock-in for most frameworks (code is portable text files). TouchDesigner projects depend on the proprietary software to run. No framework claims rights to art created with it. Export formats are standard (images, video, web).
infrastructure_governance.interoperability: Moderate to high. OSC (Open Sound Control) protocol enables real-time communication between tools. MIDI provides hardware interoperability. p5.js runs in any browser. Shader code (GLSL) is portable across frameworks. TouchDesigner can integrate with most other tools via protocols. However, each framework's project format is proprietary and non-transferable. No standard project format exists across creative coding tools.
infrastructure_governance.preservation_strategy: Variable. Code-based works (Processing, p5.js) are relatively preservable as text files but depend on runtime environments that evolve. p5.js benefits from browser ubiquity but browser APIs change. TouchDesigner projects are at-risk if Derivative ceases operations. openFrameworks projects depend on C++ compilation environments. The Processing Foundation has no formal archival program. Rhizome and similar organizations address preservation case by case.
infrastructure_governance.consent_architecture: Not applicable in the traditional sense. These are creation tools, not data collection or distribution systems. The consent question arises when creative coding tools are used to process external data (surveillance feeds, social media data, biometric input) for art projects, but this is determined by the artist's practice, not the framework.

field_position.relation_to_traditional_art_world: Parallel moving toward integration. Creative coding has gained institutional recognition: MoMA's acquisition of video games, Whitney Biennial inclusion of net art, Art Basel digital art sections. However, many institutions still struggle to exhibit, collect, and conserve code-based work. The creative coding community has its own exhibition ecosystem (SIGGRAPH Art Gallery, Ars Electronica, Eyeo Festival, Processing Community Day) that operates partly independently of the traditional art world.
field_position.what_it_enables: Art that would be impossible without computation: generative systems that produce infinite variations, real-time interactive installations, data-driven visualizations, live coded performances, algorithmic composition. Democratizes access to computational art-making (especially p5.js with zero setup in browser). Enables rapid prototyping of artistic ideas. Creates a pathway from education to professional practice.
field_position.what_it_lacks: Integrated preservation infrastructure. Standardized metadata for code-based artworks. Connection between the creation tools and the markets/institutions that might support the work. Critical frameworks adequate to the medium (most art criticism still struggles with code-based work). Accessibility features for artists with disabilities. Better support for collaborative and non-Western creative coding practices. Documentation standards that capture artistic intent alongside technical implementation.
field_position.who_is_excluded: Artists without programming literacy (despite accessibility efforts, coding remains a barrier). People without reliable internet access (for browser-based tools). Artists who cannot afford high-end GPUs (for TouchDesigner, real-time graphics). Communities where creative coding education is unavailable. Non-English speakers (documentation is predominantly English, though Processing has translation efforts). Artists whose practice is primarily material or embodied rather than computational.
field_position.frontier_signal: Established as a field, frontier at edges. The core tools are mature and stable. Frontier activity includes: AI integration (ml5.js, RunwayML plugins), Rust-based frameworks (Nannou) for performance, WebGPU for browser-based GPU computing, live coding as performance practice, and creative coding in XR/spatial computing. The field is also grappling with how generative AI changes the meaning of 'creative coding.'

attention_intention.discovery_mechanism: Education (university courses, online tutorials like The Coding Train), word of mouth, community events (Processing Community Day, creative coding meetups), social media sharing of outputs (#creativecoding, #generativeart), curated platforms (Creative Applications Network, OpenProcessing). Discovery is primarily community-driven rather than algorithm-driven.
attention_intention.attention_dependency: Low for the tools themselves. The frameworks would survive social media disappearance. The communities have pre-social-media roots (Processing predates Twitter by 5 years). However, individual artists' visibility depends on social media sharing. The generative art NFT market's attention dependency does not extend to the underlying tools.
attention_intention.intention_alignment: Strongly intention-aligned. These tools exist to serve artists' creative needs. The Processing Foundation's mission statement explicitly centers accessibility and inclusivity. No framework monetizes user attention. The tools represent infrastructure built by practitioners for practitioners.
attention_intention.commons_contribution: Very strong. Open-source code, shared libraries, community tutorials, educational resources, free workshops. The Processing Foundation explicitly operates as a commons. openFrameworks' addon ecosystem is community-contributed. Hydra's collaborative live coding ethos embodies commons values. This is one of the most commons-oriented corners of the digital art field.

provenance_temporality.provenance_type: Neither, primarily. The frameworks themselves do not track provenance. Art created with these tools may or may not have provenance systems applied (e.g., generative art minted as NFTs has ownership provenance). The creation process (code commits, iterations) could serve as provenance of artistic development but this is not formalized.
provenance_temporality.temporal_logic: Real-time and generative. The tools enable works that exist in continuous present (live coded performances), accumulate over time (generative systems), or respond to temporal inputs (data-driven installations). The temporal logic is determined by the artwork, not the framework.
provenance_temporality.absence_handling: The tools themselves do not address field absences. However, creative coding communities are increasingly aware of absences in their history: underrepresentation of non-Western practitioners, lack of documentation of early works, missing critical discourse. Projects like Processing Foundation's fellowship program attempt to address some of these gaps.

coherence.coherence_vs_consensus: Coherence. The creative coding field accommodates radically different practices (visual generative art, live coding music, interactive installations, data visualization) under a shared set of values (computation as creative medium, open sharing, accessibility). There is no consensus on what good creative coding art looks like, but there is coherence around the practice.
coherence.contestability: High. The open-source nature means anyone can fork, modify, or critique the tools. Aesthetic judgments are contested through exhibitions, publications, and community discussion. The field actively debates questions like: is AI-generated art creative coding? Does spectacle installation art represent or betray the field's values? Is commercial use (advertising, corporate events) legitimate creative coding?
coherence.forkability: Very high for open-source tools (Processing, p5.js, openFrameworks, Hydra). The code is publicly available and MIT/LGPL licensed. Multiple forks and derivatives exist. Practical barriers are low. TouchDesigner is not forkable (proprietary). The field's open-source ethos makes forkability a core value.

adai_comparison.what_adai_should_adopt: The commons-first approach: building open tools that serve practitioners rather than extracting from them. The Processing Foundation's commitment to accessibility and diversity as design principles. The community governance models that sustain projects over decades. The educational pipeline that brings new practitioners into the field. The ethos that infrastructure should be free and shared.
adai_comparison.what_adai_should_refuse: The implicit assumption that creative coding is primarily about visual output (many of these tools privilege the visual over other modes of knowing). The individual authorship model that underlies most creative coding practice. The presentism that focuses on current tools without systematic documentation of the field's history and evolution. The English-language dominance of documentation and community resources.
adai_comparison.structural_tension: Creative coding frameworks define the aesthetic vocabulary of the field through their affordances (what the tools make easy shapes what artists create). A(DAI) must understand this shaping effect without reducing art to its tools. The tension is between mapping the field as it is practiced (which requires deep understanding of toolchains) and seeing beyond tool-determined aesthetics to the broader questions of meaning, context, and cultural significance that the tools cannot capture.

regulatory_legal.regulatory_exposure: Minimal for the tools themselves. Open-source licenses (MIT, LGPL) are well-established legally. Artworks created with these tools may face regulatory issues (e.g., data-driven art using personal data falls under GDPR; AI-integrated works may be subject to EU AI Act transparency requirements). No regulation targets creative coding frameworks specifically.
regulatory_legal.ip_model: Open-source licenses (MIT, LGPL, AGPL) for most frameworks. Art created with open-source tools belongs entirely to the artist. TouchDesigner commercial license permits commercial output. No framework claims IP over work created with it. The open-source model enables maximum creative freedom.
regulatory_legal.opt_in_vs_opt_out: Opt-in: artists choose to use these tools. No data collection or consent issues at the tool level. When creative coding involves external data sources (cameras, sensors, APIs), consent questions arise at the project level.

ecosystem.platform_dependency: Varies. p5.js: depends on web browsers (highly resilient). Processing: depends on Java runtime (stable but declining). openFrameworks: depends on C++ compilers and OS-specific build tools. TouchDesigner: depends on Derivative Inc. and NVIDIA GPUs. Hydra: depends on web browsers and WebGL. Generally low single-point-of-failure risk for open-source tools, higher for proprietary ones.
ecosystem.network_effects: Moderate positive network effects through community: more users create more tutorials, libraries, and shared knowledge. The Processing/p5.js ecosystem benefits most from scale. Network effects operate through education (more courses mean more practitioners) rather than through marketplace dynamics.
ecosystem.post_crash_trajectory: Unaffected by NFT crash at the tool level. The tools predated the NFT boom and continue independently. The generative art NFT market (which heavily uses p5.js) contracted, but the underlying creative coding communities remained stable. Growing interest in creative coding education, live coding performance, and AI-integrated creative practice provides continued momentum.
